definition: Grounding explanation, also called metaphysical or constitutive explanation: what it is about a thing in virtue of which a fact obtains, as how people are acting makes an event count as a conference, in contrast to what caused it. Written 'the Xs ground Y', plural Xs and singular Y ranging over facts, which he calls a convenient shorthand for a sentential operator 'because'. He assumes it transitive and takes the notion for granted, giving no analysis (§1, pp.381-382). A fact is substantive if apt for being grounded, autonomous if not; of apt facts, brute or fundamental ones lack a ground and derivative ones have one (§§2-3, pp.383-385). Conjunctions are a paradigm of facts grounded in their conjuncts (§6, pp.392-393). His PSR: every substantive fact has an autonomous ground. Necessitarianism there: every truth is necessarily true.
